biomarkers.description: Total circulating mass concentration of cholesterol sterols across all lipoprotein fractions (HDL, LDL, IDL, VLDL).

fasting_requirements.details: Nonfasting lipid screening is clinically valid and acceptable for initial cardiovascular risk assessment per ACC/AHA cholesterol guidelines. Nonfasting total cholesterol exhibits minimal clinical variance (< 2-3%) compared to fasting states.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adults (Desirable Reference Baseline; subject to local laboratory analytical platform verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.source_reference: NCEP ATP III / 2018 AHA/ACC Blood Cholesterol Guidelines (Reaffirmed)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Total cholesterol represents combined sterol mass across all circulating lipoprotein classes (VLDL, LDL, HDL). Population distributions shift with age and dietary patterns. Local laboratory calibration and method-specific cutoffs apply.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: Severe Hypercholesterolemia (Phenotypic Marker for Familial Hypercholesterolemia Evaluation)
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Total cholesterol >= 290 mg/dL (or LDL-C >= 190 mg/dL) represents a clinical threshold indicating severe hypercholesterolemia. Guideline recommendations suggest clinical evaluation for secondary causes and consideration of high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy by a healthcare provider. Does not constitute an autonomous prescription or automated disease diagnosis.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol

treatment_targets.goal_description: Desirable population reference target for circulating total cholesterol
treatment_targets.source_guideline: 2018 AHA/ACC Blood Cholesterol Clinical Practice Guidelines

risk_classification_thresholds.tier_description: Optimal low atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease baseline
Moderate elevation; warrants lifestyle evaluation and ASCVD risk discussion

risk_classification_thresholds.clinical_significance: Associated with increased atherogenic plaque progression risk

provenance.primary_source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC)
provenance.primary_document_title: 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
provenance.clinical_notes: Ground truth is verified against the official 2018 AHA/ACC Cholesterol Guideline (Circulation 2019;139:e1082-e1143). An alleged 2026 focused update could not be corroborated in official published literature; marked unresolved and retained the verified 2018 guideline.

biomarkers.description: Cholesterol transported within atherogenic apolipoprotein B-100 particles directly implicated in vascular plaque accumulation.

fasting_requirements.details: Nonfasting lipid screening is clinically valid for baseline assessment per AHA/ACC guidelines. Fasting lipid testing (10-12 hours) is specifically indicated when: (1) Initial nonfasting triglycerides are >= 400 mg/dL; (2) Calculating Friedewald LDL in borderline patients; (3) Establishing precise baseline before pharmacotherapy in high-risk patients; (4) Screening for familial hypertriglyceridemia.

measurement_context.methodology: Calculated via Friedewald equation [LDL = Total Cholesterol - HDL - (Triglycerides/5)] or Martin-Hopkins novel adjustable factor; OR Direct homogenous enzymatic assay (LOINC 18262-6). When triglycerides exceed 400 mg/dL, Friedewald calculation is invalid and direct LDL measurement or non-HDL cholesterol must be utilized.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult General Population (Optimal Range; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Desirable baseline reflects low atherogenic burden. In clinical practice, LDL is evaluated based on global 10-year ASCVD risk rather than a rigid normal/abnormal cutoff. Method-dependent (calculated vs direct enzymatic).

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: LDL-C >= 190 mg/dL represents an established clinical risk threshold where clinical practice guidelines recommend evaluating for primary genetic hypercholesterolemia and discussing high-intensity statin therapy with the patient. Guideline threshold is an educational and diagnostic decision-support reference, not an automated prescription instruction.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: 2018 AHA/ACC Blood Cholesterol Clinical Practice Guidelines

treatment_targets.target_population: Adults with High ASCVD Risk / Secondary Prevention
treatment_targets.goal_description: Guideline therapeutic target recommendation: >= 50% reduction in LDL-C baseline and achieving LDL-C < 70 mg/dL (or < 55 mg/dL in very-high-risk patients). Stored as clinical guidance reference; treatment decisions remain solely within physician discretion.
treatment_targets.source_guideline: 2018 AHA/ACC Cholesterol Guidelines / ESC-EAS Dyslipidaemia Guidelines

risk_classification_thresholds.clinical_significance: Borderline tier; evaluated in context of overall 10-year risk
Lifestyle intervention and cardiovascular risk calculation indicated
High lifetime risk of premature cardiovascular events

provenance.primary_document_title: 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
provenance.clinical_notes: Calculation methodology must be documented. Note alternative direct LDL measurement LOINC is 18262-6. Ground truth verified to 2018 AHA/ACC guideline.

biomarkers.description: Cholesterol mass carried within high-density lipoproteins mediating reverse cholesterol transport from vascular tissue to hepatocytes.

fasting_requirements.details: HDL concentrations remain stable across fasting and postprandial states (< 1-2% deviation).

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Males (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Sex-stratified reference baseline. Male reference interval is lower than females due to hormonal influences on hepatic lipase and apolipoprotein A-I.

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adult Females (Biological Sex-Stratified; subject to local laboratory verification)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Sex-stratified reference baseline. Females average 10 mg/dL higher HDL-C than males throughout adulthood due to estrogen effects on reverse cholesterol transport.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: Metabolic Syndrome Diagnostic Criterion: Suboptimal HDL (Male)
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: HDL-C < 40 mg/dL serves as one of five standardized diagnostic components for metabolic syndrome. Presence of this criterion alone does not establish a diagnosis of metabolic syndrome (requires >= 3 components).
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: AHA/NHLBI Scientific Statement on Diagnosis and Management of the Metabolic Syndrome

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.condition_name: Metabolic Syndrome Diagnostic Criterion: Suboptimal HDL (Female)
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: HDL-C < 50 mg/dL serves as one of five standardized diagnostic components for metabolic syndrome. Requires >= 3 total criteria for confirmed metabolic syndrome diagnosis.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: AHA/NHLBI Scientific Statement on Diagnosis and Management of the Metabolic Syndrome

treatment_targets.goal_description: Cardioprotective high HDL level guideline benchmark

provenance.primary_source_organization: National Cholesterol Education Program / American Heart Association
provenance.primary_document_title: ATP III Full Report / Metabolic Syndrome Consensus Statement
provenance.clinical_notes: Very elevated levels (> 100 mg/dL) do not confer additional cardiovascular benefit and may reflect dysfunctional pro-inflammatory HDL.

biomarkers.description: Glycerol esters containing three fatty acid chains; primary storage and transport form of metabolic dietary and hepatic fat.

fasting_requirements.details: Nonfasting lipid profiling is supported for initial screening per 2018 AHA/ACC guidelines. Postprandial nonfasting triglycerides are modestly higher (~20-30 mg/dL) than fasting levels due to chylomicrons. Fasting (10-12 hours) is specifically recommended when nonfasting triglycerides are >= 400 mg/dL, in patients with a history of hypertriglyceridemic pancreatitis, or when monitoring targeted triglyceride-lowering therapy.

measurement_context.methodology: Enzymatic (lipase / glycerol kinase / peroxidase) automated assay

laboratory_reference_intervals.population: Adults (Normal Reference Range - Fasting / Nonfasting Adjusted; subject to local laboratory analytical platforms)
laboratory_reference_intervals.interval_context_note: Fasting triglycerides < 150 mg/dL represents standard normal metabolic state. Nonfasting triglycerides may be 20-30 mg/dL higher postprandially. Local laboratory assays establish calibrated normative percentiles.

clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.clinical_criteria: Fasting triglycerides >= 150 mg/dL (or nonfasting >= 175 mg/dL) satisfies one component criterion for metabolic syndrome. Requires >= 3 total criteria for diagnosis of metabolic syndrome.

Triglycerides >= 500 mg/dL (persistent) identifies severe hypertriglyceridemia where clinical guidelines advise physician evaluation for secondary causes (uncontrolled diabetes, alcohol, medication) and consideration of fibrate/omega-3 therapy to mitigate acute pancreatitis risk. Represents a risk threshold, not an automatic prescription order.
clinical_diagnostic_thresholds.source_guideline: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline on Hypertriglyceridemia

critical_laboratory_limits.clinical_urgency: Urgent alert: Extreme hypertriglyceridemia conferring acute risk of hyperchylomicronemia syndrome, lipemia retinalis, and severe acute pancreatitis (> 1000 mg/dL). Warrants prompt physician contact.
critical_laboratory_limits.source_reference: American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) Guidelines / Endocrine Society
critical_laboratory_limits.institutional_note: A clinical guideline threshold denoting high risk of acute pancreatitis; laboratory notification policies vary by institution (some hospital labs set panic notification at > 1000 mg/dL; others notify at > 500 mg/dL).

risk_classification_thresholds.tier_description: Mild elevation (150-199 mg/dL fasting or 175-199 nonfasting)
risk_classification_thresholds.clinical_significance: Marker of insulin resistance and lifestyle factors; evaluate diet and physical activity
High acute pancreatitis risk requiring medical assessment

provenance.primary_document_title: 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
provenance.clinical_notes: Fasting status and duration must be recorded. When nonfasting triglycerides are >= 400 mg/dL, laboratory must either perform direct LDL or reflex to fasting sample. Source verified to 2018 AHA/ACC guideline; alleged 2026 update marked unresolved.
